- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underreact to upward momentum — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior 5d), model often overcorrects downward — reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% for next 5–7d.
- If official supply net is negative and bullish events outnumber bearish, model underestimates upside — add 2–4% bias to forecast mean for 30d.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from 0.00 to 1.00) and model doesn’t adjust, forecast may lag — apply 1–2% lag correction to early 5d.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and supply net is negative, model often overestimates downside — cap forecast decline at 1–2% below historical low.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model tends to underestimate peak — add 3–5% upward bias to 10–15d horizon.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bearish spikes (e.g., -1.00) followed by recovery, model often fails to anticipate reversal — add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to 15–20d.
